title: Minimax Rates for Randomized Predeath Count Contrasts under Repeated Independent Inspections
banked_reason: D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.8 < 7.4, so graded tier subfield is capped at incremental; the uniform unknown-censor product-limit remainder is unproved.
gap_reasons: The matched frontier is not fully proved for the advertised unknown-censoring class because the load-bearing censor-score lemma skips the central product-limit argument: bounds (6)–(7) are asserted from informal grouping rather than derived.

Without a corrected uniform expansion, the data-only upper risk bound and the 90%-honest interval coverage are unestablished, leaving the full-panel converse and the known-censor split-visit calculation as the secure contribution.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a full-panel lower-bound construction and a known-censor split-score upper calculation, then attempted a reverse-Kaplan–Meier correction for unknown censoring. The reviewer found an invalid tied-atom risk set; a later repair corrected the observable construction but still asserted the nonlinear random-denominator remainder needed for the upper-risk and honest-interval theorems. The fixed 0<beta<1 unknown-censor frontier remains open, as does the separate beta=1 endpoint.
tldr: For each fixed \(0<\beta<1\), independent repeat inspections yield the matched minimax absolute-risk and uniformly honest connected-interval-length rate \(n^{-1/2}\vee(nJ^{\beta+1})^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}\) for the randomized predeath count contrast, uniformly over \(1\le J\le n\). One observable split-visit procedure attains the upper bounds on the broad class with arbitrary within-subject dependence and unknown independent censoring; its reverse Kaplan--Meier nuisance uses a deaths-first tied-atom risk and is controlled only after integration against the complete-death score. The full-panel converse already holds in the homogeneous reverse-mean subclass \(m(a,u,0)-m(a,u,s)=\Lambda_a(s)\). At root-\(n\) saturation the local experiment is nuisance-indexed and nonunique, so exact leading constants require a residual least-favorable nuisance optimization; the \(\beta=1\) calculation remains supporting only.
gap: Fixed mixed-case interval-censoring theory and bounded-visit reverse-mean panel-count theory do not determine the minimax point-risk and uniformly honest expected-length law for a randomized predeath count contrast when \(J\) grows and death-specific count laws are otherwise unrestricted.
fill: For fixed \(0<\beta<1\), a single split-visit estimator and score-corrected interval attain the growing-visit frontier, and a one-jump full-panel likelihood gives matching point-risk and honest-length converses together with the exact root-\(n\) saturation threshold.
